clue.text: Patient with trapped heel causing fall

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a doctor's patient is a case
a heel is a cad, a man who behaves badly

explanation.surface: A patient who has caught a heel somewhere takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like part of the foot, but here it is a scoundrel, an old-fashioned word for a man who treats others badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, a fall of water down rocks in steps.

clue.text: Provider of clothing more comfortable around the middle

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: cosier means more comfortable
the tum is the stomach, the middle of the body

explanation.surface: A tailor makes clothes that are looser at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle' is the belly, not the centre letter of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, such as theatrical outfits, so provides clothing.

clue.text: Extremely doubtful ingredients of southern vintage exposing deception

indicators.note: at the extremes means at the two ends, so only the outer letters of the word are used
ingredients go inside a mixture, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a vintage is a wine of a particular year
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dubious wine label reveals fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingredients' sounds like part of a recipe, which the wine picture supports, but it signals letters placed inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fraud or con, an act of deception to cheat someone.

clue.text: Down payment covering openers of new accounts to accommodate lenders before delivery

indicators.note: an opener comes at the start, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: an ante is a stake put down before a hand of poker
the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A bank deposit sweetening the terms for new customers, before the goods arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'covering' means sitting on top of, so ANTE comes first. 'Openers' covers five words in a row, not just the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal care happens before a baby is born, and delivery is the birth itself.

clue.text: City House making a comeback

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
Ho is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A financial firm returns to the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a comeback' looks like a reversal signal, but nothing is reversed: 'comeback' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound that bounces off a surface and returns, a comeback of the original noise.

clue.text: Made a mark, reportedly, from money advanced

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: to make a mark on something is to have impressed it

explanation.surface: Someone left a mark after being given a cash advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a sum of money advanced to an employee or official to cover expenses, as in an imprest account.

clue.text: Render weak, though alive and kicking when it is injected

indicators.note: a drug injected goes into the body, so these letters go inside the others
kicking things about scatters them, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is said to weaken a patient who is nonetheless lively once injected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alive and kicking' is a stock phrase, but 'kicking' is the signal to mix the letters with IT added.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate an argument is to make it void or ineffective, to weaken its force.

clue.text: South American worker's entertaining run for President

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them in your home, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: a peon is a Latin American labourer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Latin American labourer is amused by a campaign for the presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run for President' reads as an election bid; R goes inside PEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was President of Argentina, elected in 1946 and again in 1973.

clue.text: Issue a note in support of call up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Send out a memo backing someone's summons.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'in support of' puts A and TE underneath the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out or flow forth, which is what emanate means.

clue.text: Souvenir from old Kent building

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from the materials, so the letters are put together afresh

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keepsake from an ancient building in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a noun, a historic building in Kent, a county of south-east England; it is a verb telling us to construct.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a keepsake or memento kept as a reminder, so a souvenir.

clue.text: Riddle surrounding Welsh author

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: to riddle is to pass through a sieve, to sift
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a writer from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' suggests a puzzle, but it is the verb meaning to sieve. 'Welsh author' reads as one phrase; Welsh only gives the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels, is a famous author.

clue.text: Hard to maintain rifle in such a holder

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to aver is to maintain or assert
to rifle a town is to sack or plunder it

explanation.surface: It is difficult to keep a rifle in a bag made to carry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like the gun of the surface, but it is a verb meaning to plunder. The definition leans on the whole clue: a holder for the things just described.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a canvas bag carried on the back or shoulder, used by soldiers and walkers to hold supplies.

clue.text: Neglected fellow in a Parisian environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever is placed in it, so the French word encloses the other

blocks.note: une is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man left ignored while living in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: A college fellow at Oxford or Cambridge is called a don.
explanation.definitionFit: Work left undone has been neglected, not attended to or finished.

clue.text: Fruit harvested by worker in level country

indicators.note: a crop gathered in by someone is held within their grasp, so one word goes inside

blocks.note: a plain is flat, level land
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Farmhands bring in a fruit crop on flat land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harvested' fits the fruit picture, but it tells us one word is gathered inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy tropical fruit related to the banana, usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Common lawman in the flying squad?

blocks.note: first meaning: old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform
second meaning: a big buzzing fly, one of a squad that flies

explanation.surface: A rank-and-file officer in the Flying Squad, the Metropolitan Police's robbery unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' signals slang rather than a legal term. The Flying Squad is Scotland Yard's armed robbery unit; the question mark admits that here it means flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is old slang for a policeman and also names a large blue blowfly.

clue.text: Still a popular monarch? Exactly!

blocks.note: something in fashion is in
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to a T means exactly

explanation.surface: Is the Queen still well liked? Absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb 'yet', but it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert lies motionless, without power to move or act, as a still object does.

clue.text: Old men get shaky in footing

indicators.note: something shaky is unsteady and wobbles out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly men become unsteady on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is part of the letters to mix, not an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is a secure foothold or position gained, especially by troops, so a footing.

clue.text: Relaxing treatment for oilmen let loose

indicators.note: let loose, the letters run free and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Rig workers given time off get a soothing massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' is part of the letters, not a link; only 'loose' signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a softening, soothing preparation, something that relaxes skin or tension.

clue.text: Advocates getting in money to build large food store

indicators.note: getting into something means being taken inside it, so one item sits within another

blocks.note: tin is slang for money
barristers collectively are the Bar

explanation.surface: Lawyers raise funds to put up a big grocery warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BAR goes inside TIN. Tithes were a tenth of farm produce paid to the church, stored in such barns.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn is a large medieval barn built to hold the produce given to the church as tithes.

clue.text: Disgusting insecticide

blocks.note: first meaning: offensive, causing aversion
second meaning: a substance that keeps insects away

explanation.surface: A grumble about a nasty bug spray.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a repellent drives insects off rather than killing them, but the looser sense is fair in a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something revolting and a noun for a spray that drives off insects.

clue.text: Smother with dressing

blocks.note: first meaning: to coat thickly
second meaning: a sticking ... put over a wound

explanation.surface: An instruction to cover a salad with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests salad dressing; it is a wound dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for covering something thickly and a noun for an adhesive bandage.

clue.text: Fledgling's cry of pain when meeting obstacle?

blocks.note: ow is what you shout when hurt
a let is an old word for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A baby bird squeaks as it bumps into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. LET as obstacle survives in tennis and in passports.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so a fledgling bird.

clue.text: Advancing Russian general at the front captures five hundred

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which is all that is used
something captured is held inside, so one letter is taken within the others

blocks.note: Lenin, the Russian revolutionary leader
the first letter of the word
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A Russian general on the front line advances and takes five hundred prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian general' reads as one person, but they are separate: Lenin, then the G of general. D goes inside LENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending money is advancing it, handing over a loan to be repaid.

clue.text: Father gets suit -- or part of it

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
a lawsuit is an action in court

explanation.surface: Dad receives a whole suit of clothes, or just a piece of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is a legal suit. The definition 'part of it' refers back to the whole just built.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a part or portion of a whole, the piece of something larger.

clue.text: Cheeky novel

blocks.note: first meaning: impudent, too forward
second meaning: new, original

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, perhaps an anagram signal, but it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means impertinent towards someone and also new or not seen before.

clue.text: Crown jewels

blocks.note: surface reading: the royal regalia kept in the Tower of London
setter's reading: a jewelled headpiece, a crown made of jewels

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like the Tower of London's royal collection, but read as 'jewels forming a crown' it describes one ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band or coronet worn on the head, a small crown studded with gems.

clue.text: Throw oneself into exercises without a breather

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word is placed around the other

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
a lung is an organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: Diving into a workout without stopping for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a breather' reads as 'with no rest', but without here means outside. 'Into' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge into something is to throw yourself into it suddenly and wholeheartedly.

clue.text: No opening for goods in old vessel

indicators.note: with no opening, the first letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: cargo is the goods a ship carries

explanation.surface: A wrecked ship's hold has no way in for the freight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo is the ship of Greek myth in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed for the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo is the legendary ship of Jason, an ancient vessel from Greek myth.

clue.text: Dentist perhaps sees more decay about to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: extra means more
rot is decay
c, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A dentist finds more tooth decay at a return visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two pieces go backwards; the first stays as it is. 'Perhaps' marks a dentist as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist pulling teeth is one who extracts things, so an example of an extractor.

clue.text: Little boy accompanied by a girl

blocks.note: Eric is a boy's name; 'Eric, or Little by Little' is a Victorian school story
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small boy goes along with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' adds to the surface; a boy's name is all that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's first name, so a girl as crosswords use the word.

clue.text: Leaves kill in this place

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other here

blocks.note: here means in this place
a hunter bags a bird by killing it

explanation.surface: An order to kill on the spot, or someone departing a killing ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is green vegetation, the grass and leafy plants of a pasture.

clue.text: Angular figure can go to ruin

indicators.note: something gone to ruin has fallen apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: A figure with sharp corners can fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to ruin' reads as one phrase, but 'to' belongs with the letters being mixed; 'ruin' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided polygon, a plane figure full of angles.
